newsitem.title: HUNGARY: HUNGARY PAYOUT HOPES BOOST TO NEW HIGHS.
newsitem.headline: HUNGARY PAYOUT HOPES BOOST TO NEW HIGHS.

text.p: Shares in Hungarian chemicals firm TVK Rt were leaping more than three percent to a new record high in early Wednesday trading as the market takes an imminent payout by the state to TVK for granted.
"Everybody takes this for sure," one trader said.
In early trading TVK shares rallied to a new record high of 3,330 forints. At 0950 GMT it traded at 3,320, up 120.
TVK shares have been heading upwards recently on market expectations that APV will decide today on paying out some billion forints plus another one billion in interest to TVK.
A 1989 law promised state-owned companies which transformed themselved into shareholder companies before 1992 that they would receive 20 percent of all subsequent privatisation revenues.
An APV press official on Wednesday confirmed to Reuters Monday's information that the payouts were not on the preliminiary agenda of APV's board meeting today.
"But the agenda may change in the very last minute," she said, adding that the board has already started its meeting.
APV will hold a news conference about its decision at 1300 GMT.
The payouts, if materialise, are expected to positively affect TVK's first half earnings.

Analysts said earlier that the payments may affect many of the BSE's leading companies, including oil and gas company MOL, pharmaceuticals Egis, tile maker Zalakeramia, meat processor Pick and OTP Bank.
